sa8:0.3: 11-14 (8). The Past Is Impermanent, Painful, Empty, and Not Self
sa8:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa8:2.1: It was then that the Bhagavān addressed the monks,
sa8:2.2: “Past and future form are [11] impermanent … [12] painful … [13] empty … [14] not self, so why wouldn’t that be for present form?
sa8:2.3: Noble disciples who observe them in this way don’t look back to past form or wish for future form.
sa8:2.4: Regarding present form, they become disillusioned, free of desire, and headed straight to its cessation.
sa8:3.1: “Thus, past and future feeling … conception … volition … awareness are [11] impermanent … [12] painful … [13] empty … [14] not self, so why wouldn’t that be for present awareness?
sa8:3.2: Noble disciples who observe them in this way don’t look back to past awareness or wish for future awareness.
sa8:3.3: Regarding present awareness, they become disillusioned, free of desire, and headed straight to its cessation.”
sa8:4.1: (Like “impermanent,” “pain,” “emptiness,” and “not self” are taught in the same way.)
sa8:5.1: When the monks heard what the Buddha taught, they rejoiced and approved.
